prompt: Populate a JToolBar with named buttons and manage a JComboBox through its DefaultComboBoxModel, including the surprise that adding the first entry selects it. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: JToolBar is just a container, so adding a button is an ordinary add call and counting them means filtering getComponents() -- a toolbar can also hold separators and other components, which is why the instanceof test matters. The combo box, by contrast, is a model-driven component: DefaultComboBoxModel owns the entries, and getIndexOf returning -1 is the standard absence test used by addFont, selectFont and removeFont alike. Its habit of auto-selecting the first element it receives catches people out, because the selection changes as a side effect of adding data. Setting each button's name as well as its text is what lets a test find it by name without depending on layout order.
hints: JButton has a setName separate from its text -- set both to the same label so the tests can find it.
toolBar.getComponents() returns every child, so count only the ones where c instanceof JButton.
fonts.getIndexOf(name) returns -1 when the entry is absent. That one check drives addFont (only add when absent), selectFont (only select when present) and removeFont (report presence).
